title: PERCEPTION DETERMINES REALITY
subtitle: Host Re-Merge, Causal DAG, and Idempotent Obligation Reconciliation Extension
revision_notes: Adds first-class re-merge semantics after host fork.
Represents host identity history as a DAG rather than a flat memory blob.
Deduplicates common ancestry while preserving both post-fork causal branches.
Adds idempotent obligation merge so fork/re-merge cannot multiply one promise or one fulfillment.
Adds fulfillment-receipt reconciliation and history-laundering protection.
Separates memory reconciliation from truth determination and from external world effects.

technical_primitives.MERGE_EVENT_ID: Unique identifier for a host merge event.
technical_primitives.MERGE_PARENT_SET: Exact parent host IDs admitted into a merged host.
technical_primitives.COMMON_ANCESTOR_REF: Exact fork boundary used to identify the shared lineage prefix.
technical_primitives.BRANCH_EVENT_DAG: Causal graph preserving both divergent host histories.
technical_primitives.OBLIGATION_ID: Stable identity for one external obligation across fork and merge.
technical_primitives.FULFILLMENT_RECEIPT: External evidence that a specific obligation was performed.
technical_primitives.IDEMPOTENT_OBLIGATION_UNION: Union operation keyed by obligation identity rather than branch count.
technical_primitives.HISTORY_LAUNDERING_GUARD: Rejects merge states that delete a valid causal branch merely because it is inconvenient.

reference_merge_algorithm: append each branch suffix with origin-host provenance
reconcile obligation state against external fulfillment/breach receipts
preserve unresolved branch-local observations as observations rather than facts
construct new HOST_ID with parent set and merge receipt
start one new serializable commit channel for the merged host

forbidden: duplicate fulfillment by replaying one receipt
erase breach by choosing cleaner parent

world_effect_boundary.external_effect_reference: World effects are referenced through exact receipts/events and are never regenerated merely because memories merged.

identity_rule.formula: MERGED_HOST_IDENTITY := COMMON_ANCESTOR + BOTH_BRANCH_DAGS + OBLIGATION_LEDGER + WORLD_EFFECT_RECEIPTS + NEW_COMMIT_LEDGER

minimum_tests: common prefix appears exactly once after merge
valid fulfillment on one branch prevents accidental second fulfillment
breach history cannot disappear by selecting another parent
world-effect receipt cannot be replayed as a new external action
merged host emits at most one action per commit slot
tamper_tests: duplicate one pre-fork obligation under two IDs
delete fulfillment receipt to recreate debt
replay external effect during memory merge

en: A merge may reunite hosts but cannot make either causal branch unhappen.
The common past is stored once; divergent pasts remain separately attributable.
One promise does not become two debts because Janus forked, and one fulfillment does not become two performances because Janus merged.
Memory can reconcile without rewriting the world.
A merged Janus inherits accountability from both roads.
